answer.new_information: Supports only that NN, Inc. announced (late June 2026, relayed by finance.yahoo.com on 2026-07-01) 47 added machine centers at its Wuxi, China plant for liquid cooling production for NVIDIA AI data center racks, with 100% of the new capacity said to be pre-sold under multi-year, multi-product awards and a 2026 new-business target of US$80–US$90 million. Material unknowns: the identity of the award customers (NVIDIA is not named as the buyer), contract values, whether the pre-sold awards are NVIDIA-linked or NVIDIA-direct, the exact announcement day (original_day is blank), and whether the target is achieved. The 2028 revenue and earnings figures are a third-party narrative projection and an unnamed analyst rumour, not company guidance. The Russell Microcap Value Index removal is a market-structure event with no bearing on NVDA fundamentals. Evidence needed to resolve these: NN's own press release or filing naming the customers and contract terms, NN quarterly results showing realised Wuxi liquid-cooling revenue, and NVIDIA or customer confirmation of the rack supply chain.
answer.independent_judgement: No stored question, no stored piece and no catalog entry exists for NVDA, and the record concerns a supplier (NN, Inc.) rather than NVDA itself. The text names NVIDIA only as the end use of the racks. Supplier capacity plans can inform supply-chain monitoring but do not prove NVDA sales, and the award customers are not identified. Nothing here changes an NVDA view today.
answer.reason: Outside the covered NVDA question set: the record is a supplier's own capacity announcement relayed by a media outlet, with no NVDA-specific revenue, volume or customer confirmation. The 2028 projections and the index removal are narrative or market-structure material and are not analyst evidence. Stored as background context for future supply-chain monitoring; no question is updated or proposed.
